campaign.title: M1 lower-cone squarefree-kernel linearization gate

resource_policy.literature_policy: Use primary results on additive twists of divisor-type coefficients, quadratic-irrational linear phases, squarefree-supported exponential sums, Pell or continued-fraction exceptional sets, and bilinear forms only after deriving the exact squarefree-kernel coefficient, parity, cone inequality, mask, and dyadic power ledger. Record theorem number, coefficient class, smoothing, frequency uniformity, Diophantine hypothesis, exceptional denominators, complex-direction placement, and the complete R-M-s-t capacity.

frozen_target.question: Does the unique squarefree-kernel decomposition m=s t^2 convert the Round-144 strict large-displacement cone survivor into a target-safe large-square tail plus a source-legal fixed-centre linear-twist problem that can be proved, or into a strictly smaller owner-complete survivor; if not, what is the first exact coefficient, parity, Diophantine, exceptional-fibre, source-hypothesis, or capacity obstruction?
frozen_target.reference_formula: Let R=X^(1/4), N=floor X, C(m)=sum_(hr=m,r odd,r>4h)chi_4(r), k_m=floor(sqrt(Nm)+1/2), and j_m=k_m^2-Nm. The exact open Round-144 scalar is T_N=sum_M sum_(m in I_M, |j_m|>M^(3/4)) m^(-3/4)V_low(R^2m/N)C(m)e(sqrt(Nm)). Write every m uniquely as m=s t^2 with s squarefree, so e(sqrt(Nm))=e(t sqrt(Ns)). The target is T_N<<_epsilon X^epsilon uniformly for every real X.
quantities: The m=s t^2 decomposition is a bijection, but no cancellation follows until C(s t^2), the odd-r condition, the strict cone, and the large-displacement mask are parameterized exactly.

A candidate absolute lemma is that the aggregate part t>=M^(1/4) is target-safe, since a fixed t supports O(M/t^2) squarefree kernels on a block and the m^(-3/4) divisor envelope gives a tail of order M^(1/4)sum_(t>=M^(1/4))t^(-2). This must be proved with half-open blocks, profiles, exact radicals, and all endpoints.
On the remaining t<M^(1/4), one has s comparable to M/t^2 and hence s>M^(1/2) up to block constants. This support fact is not a signed estimate.

The identity |j_m|=|k_m-t sqrt(Ns)|(k_m+t sqrt(Ns)) translates the Round-144 mask into a nearest-integer condition on t sqrt(Ns). Exact resonance occurs only in the separately owned squarefree kernel of N; quadratic-irrational and Pell-near-resonant fibres remain possible.

The t=1 layer and every small-t layer must be retained. A bound that gains only from large t, assumes bounded continued-fraction quotients uniformly in Ns, or treats squarefree support as random is invalid.
The individual complex direction e(+t sqrt(Ns)) must be estimated. A cosine, conjugate-pair, mean-square-in-N, or average-over-s theorem is not a fixed-centre substitute.

Round 144 already parks Appell completion, rational-mode truncation, derivative-arc inference, and reciprocal stationary self-return. This round must exploit the new squarefree-kernel interface rather than relabel an invertible transform.

The Round-138 collar-tail cross owner remains independent. No result here alone proves lower GAR, either direct M1 parent, M9-M1, any M2 owner, endpoint uniformity, M9, the bridge, or a global exponent.

completion_criteria: Derive the exact bijective parameterization of C(s t^2), including every squarefree common factor, ordered factorization of s, parity restriction, chi_4 sign, strict cone inequality, and multiplicity.
Prove or refute the target-safe aggregate deletion t>=M^(1/4), with the literal profile, half-open block endpoints, exact-radical overlap, divisor powers, and dyadic summation retained.
Translate |j_m|>M^(3/4) exactly into the nearest-integer geometry of t sqrt(Ns), including the sign of j, tie convention, exact rational fibre, and Pell or continued-fraction near resonances.
For t<M^(1/4), derive the strongest lawful linear-twist, bilinear, hyperbola, or squarefree-supported estimate for the actual C(s t^2) coefficient in the individual complex direction.

Audit primary source theorems against the exact coefficient, squarefree support, t and s ranges, smoothing, frequency and centre uniformity, exceptional denominators, and complete R-M-s-t power ledger.
Test t=1, bounded t, t near M^(1/4), the exact squarefree kernel of N, distinct Pell-near-resonant kernels, even N and even s, squareful centres, and the largest active dyadic block analytically.

Prove the fixed-centre target, produce a strictly smaller owner-complete squarefree-kernel survivor with its complement target-safe, or identify the first rigorous coefficient/Diophantine/source/capacity obstruction without upgrading an upper price to a lower bound.
Close under exactly one label: target_bound, strict_squarefree_kernel_reduction, or squarefree_kernel_linearization_no_go.

review_seams.requirement: The m=s t^2 decomposition and every divisor-pair parameter, common squarefree factor, parity, character, cone inequality, and multiplicity are exact.
Any large-square tail is bounded with literal half-open blocks, profiles, exact-radical overlap, divisor weights, terminal truncation, and dyadic assembly.
The j-mask, sign, nearest-integer tie, exact squarefree kernel, and Pell/continued-fraction near resonances are distinguished exactly.
Every small-t estimate and cited theorem uses the actual C(s t^2), squarefree support, individual complex direction, fixed centre, and stated uniform parameter range.
All R, M, s, t, endpoint, mask, and complement powers are explicit, and a strict survivor is claimed only after its complement is target-safe.
Only the Round-144 lower-cone survivor may change; the independent cross owner, direct M1, all M2, endpoint, M9, bridge, and exponent claims retain their owners.

closing_assessment.main_result: Two exact multiplicity-one formulas for C(s t^2) were proved. The aggregate t>=ceil(M^(1/4)) is target-safe, leaving the strict owner t<M^(1/4), s>M^(1/2) with the original displacement mask. A literal slowly rotating exceptional family and the nonzero t=1 prime layer rule out a uniform frequency-gap or large-t-only closure; the audited source theorems do not match the coefficient, direction, uniformity, and target power simultaneously.
